incidentbot: PagerDuty triggered -> prod-redis-proxy-error-rate (us-west-2) — 120 errors/min, 3% error rate over 3m. Incident: <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-78910|PD-78910> :rotating_light:
Priya G: Acked, I'm on it.
Evan L: Thanks — any idea if customers are seeing failures?
Priya G: Quick check: frontend 5xxs are flat. Looks isolated to the canary proxy pool. No external spikes in SLO alerts.
Maya R: I see a brief spike in connection resets on redis-proxy-az-b. CPU/memory normal.
Priya G: Rolling a canary throttle for traffic -> `kubectl patch svc canary-proxy -p '{\"spec\":{\"trafficPercent\":10}}'`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary throttle applied by Priya G (revision 9f2a).
Evan L: Nice. Any logs showing upstream redis errors or timeouts?
Priya G: grep looks like transient `ECONNRESET` from the proxy to redis replicas, ~30s window. No sustained reconnect loops.
Maya R: Also saw a single autoscaler bump around same time; might have briefly cycled a pod in that AZ.
incidentbot: PagerDuty auto-resolved PD-78910 — alert cleared (error rate returned to baseline). Reason: transient connection resets; autoscaler pod churn likely.
Priya G: Confirming metrics back to normal. No customer-facing errors observed.
Evan L: Cool. Can we relax alert noise? 120/min with no customer impact seems noisy.
Priya G: Agreed — I'll open a follow-up to tune the alert to 5m sustained or add a canary-only filter.
Maya R: Suggest adding an autoscaler-safety-label filter to avoid transient churn from causing PD pages.
Priya G: Filing issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321 — will propose thresholds and a canary tag exemption.
Evan L: Thanks — mark resolved if no more activity. :+1:
Priya G: Closing thread. Will loop in oncall-runbook if we adjust thresholds.
ops-bot: note: incident PD-78910 was resolved automatically; owners: platform-infra.
